Supreme Court orders probe into deaths at Manipur relief camps

The Supreme Court of India ordered a probe into deaths that occurred in relief camps in Manipur. The Court asked for a comprehensive report on the deaths, questioning the adequacy of post‑mortem examinations and the compensation provided to families. One report said a total of 34 people had died in the camps, while another specified 25 deaths classified as unnatural. The Court’s directive includes scrutiny of the post‑mortem procedures and the compensation process. The request for a detailed investigation reflects ongoing concerns about the conditions in the camps. No further action or outcome has been reported yet.
